jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Formerly Fancy
seedTermsUsed: A loss of prestige or wealth
jokes.joke: I took my dog to a discount animal groomer called Formerly Fancy Pets. You could tell the place had fallen on hard times because the receptionist whispered, “We used to do show dogs,” while cutting a coupon off my Labrador. My dog came out with uneven bangs and the expression of a CEO who now has to wear the mascot costume.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Career Pivot
jokes.joke: I used to be a hedge fund manager. Now I'm a dog groomer. People think that's a fall from grace. It's not — I'm still trimming portfolios, they just bark now. Honestly the clients are better. A poodle has never once asked me to explain cryptocurrency at a dinner party. And when a golden retriever is unhappy with my performance, it doesn't sue me, it just bites my hand, which, frankly, is more honest feedback than I ever got in finance.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Crypto Florist
seedTermsUsed: A loss of prestige or wealth
jokes.joke: I lost my entire life savings in crypto last year. Went from a high-rise corner office to arranging bouquets at a local flower shop. My parents are devastated by the drop in prestige, but honestly? The business model is exactly the same. Guys come in in a total panic, hand me way too much money, and I give them something that's guaranteed to be dead in three days.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Humbled Ambitions
seedTermsUsed: A loss of prestige or wealth
jokes.joke: I used to be so ambitious, folks. Big dreams, power suits, corner office – I was gonna conquer everything. Then life served up a brutal loss of prestige and wealth. One bad quarter and suddenly I'm the guy whose LinkedIn is just sad. Now I stand here telling jokes, praying you laugh hard enough to cover my ramen budget. Turns out the only empire I built was this pile of 'what ifs' in my parents' basement.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Prestige Problems
seedTermsUsed: A loss of prestige or wealth
jokes.joke: I knew I’d hit a real loss of prestige when my bank called to say my credit score was now considered “anxious.” I tried to cheer myself up by taking my dog to the groomer, but even she looked at me and said, “Sir… he can’t be the only one getting a trim today.”

scores.comment: Solid finance-to-grooming turn with several usable tags, though it runs a bit long and the final bite is more clever than explosive.
Clean premise, strong parallel between crypto panic and flower-shop panic, and a sharp final line that carries the laugh.
Mostly a sad status monologue with prompt terms stated directly; it lacks a real comic turn or memorable punchline.
A compact, understandable joke with a decent double meaning on “trim,” but the setup is thin and the payoff is mild.
Clean escalation from discount groomer to CEO-in-mascot-costume image; solid but not surprising turn.
Crypto-to-flowers analogy lands well; the 'dead in three days' closer actually carries the laugh.
Familiar fallen-ambition/basement tropes; punchline restates the premise rather than turning it.
Nice 'anxious' credit score personification; groomer tag is clever but slightly unclear as a standalone closer.
Strong final image and good stage rhythm. Beautifully weaves the two seed concepts together without relying on exact wording.
Violates the prompt constraints by incorporating a third seed concept ('loss of prestige' via 'fall from grace'), and relies heavily on safe, generic corporate comparisons.
Suffers from heavy prompt recitation, forcing the exact seed phrases rather than conceptualizing them, and falls back on tired stand-up clichés.
The 'anxious' credit score is a clever premise and the punchline lands solidly, though the opening awkwardly recites the prompt verbatim.
Solid premise with vivid dog/CEO image; good escalation but punchline mildly predictable.
Clean finance-to-groomer transition with honest feedback bite; relies on familiar tropes.
Tight premise, strong relatable punchline equating bouquets to crypto; natural delivery.
Cute anxious credit score setup but groomer punchline feels forced and mild.
Solid premise with a clear turn; mildly funny and cleanly written.
Consistent humor and relatable comparisons; leans familiar but works.
Strong premise, clean escalation, and a sharp final line.
More confessional than joke; lacks a distinct turn and uses only one seed concept clearly.
